title: iOS Metal: transparent lighting loss after sky rendering; binding-cache risk persists in 4.8 dev7
body:
### 4.8 release triage request (updated 2026-10-05)

Please consider investigating and fixing this iOS Metal transparent-lighting regression **before Godot 4.8 stable**, and assigning the **4.8 milestone** if the rendering team confirms the diagnosis. It affects visible character overlays and transparent water in our tested scenes and currently requires a native-engine patch and App relink.

The latest published 4.8 development snapshot is [4.8 dev7](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/tag/4.8-dev7), engine commit `c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f`. I rechecked its official source and the current master commit `e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083` on 2026-10-05:

- [dev7 render-pipeline changes still leave cache invalidation commented out](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L411-L420).
- [dev7 push constants still write encoder buffer slots outside BindingCache](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L1042-L1049), while [direct uniform binding still uses the cache](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L1245-L1249).
- At the checked [master commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L411-L420), both `metal3_objects.cpp` and `metal3_objects.h` are byte-identical to dev7. The `.cpp` SHA-256 is `05064ac772ee73a19eaa60c31a817a5be5505f7d5590557cc16028662b407cf8`.

**Evidence boundary:** this identifies a persisting source-level risk in the 4.8 branch. Physical-device failure/fix A/B evidence below is from 4.7.1. Neither unpatched 4.8 dev7 nor current master has yet been run on our iPhone, and the newly reduced standalone diagnostic still needs device validation. Please review whether full cache invalidation or a more targeted slot-aware solution is appropriate for 4.8.

### Tested versions

- Reproduced on a physical iPhone with Godot 4.7.1.stable, commit a13da4feb8d8aefc283c3763d33a2f170a18d541, Mobile renderer / Metal. The failing baseline uses the unmodified Metal engine object from the exported native library.
- On the same device, restoring binding_cache.clear() in MDCommandBuffer::bind_pipeline fixes the tested transparent-water and original transparent next_pass cases. The face A/B uses identical PCK bytes and replaces only the metal3_objects native archive member.
- Source review only: 4.7.2 (ed1daf0bf) has identical metal3_objects.cpp and .h to 4.7.1; 4.8 dev7 (c971f93e7) still comments out this invalidation and retains the relevant binding logic. These records do NOT establish unpatched physical-device reproduction on those versions.
- 4.6.1 source clears the cache on render-pipeline changes; the exact first affected version has not been bisected.

### System information

Physical iPhone 11, Apple A13 (arm64), iOS 26.6.1, Metal backend, Mobile renderer. Control: Android API 36.1 arm64 emulator, Vulkan / Mobile (not an Android physical-device test).

### Issue description

Transparent objects can lose their directional-light contribution after a sky draw on iOS Metal, while opaque objects and ambient-only lighting remain correct. This affects both a water material with ALPHA = 0.8 and the original layered transparent next_pass face materials in our project. Expected: transparent objects retain directional lighting, with their contribution blended according to alpha.

### Previously completed device isolation tests

The scene keeps the real sky/environment and a visible DirectionalLight3D. Disabling ambient light and reflections isolates the direct contribution. Glow is disabled for numerical comparisons.

| Control / sample | Unmodified Metal object, iPhone | Cache invalidation restored, same iPhone | Android Vulkan emulator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original transparent water, direct light only | #6a737b (effectively no direct light) | #7194c0 | #7194c0 |
| StandardMaterial3D alpha control, direct light only | #6a737b | #7396c2 | not recorded for this variant |
| Transparent water, direct light only, sky drawing disabled | #819bc0 | #819bc0 | not recorded for this variant |
| Transparent water, sky ambient only | #6d8fda | not needed for this control | #6d8fda |

Removing ALPHA so the original water enters the opaque queue produces matching iPhone/Android results. Keeping ALPHA = 1.0 in the transparent queue still fails. Removing normals or shadows does not fix the defect. Disabling the sky background draw restores direct lighting without the native patch. The no-sky color is a separate background/compositing control, not a same-background color comparison.

### Native-engine A/B with identical PCK

On the same iPhone and isolated bundle, the original ten-layer transparent next_pass face loses its eye whites/highlights with the unmodified engine object, and renders normally after only replacing the native Metal object. An opaque composed face renders normally with both engines.

Both runs use PCK SHA-256 `e1b1f038dd84d75131be2bb1a33cb499c2ae47d060831662ef3420a9b5f145f9`. Executable SHA-256 values:
- Unmodified: `71d721484cafa8c7d15074b0735b6ac90aa9f694ad6b5681434c2afa16c649ca`
- Patched: `0f8eb52d46fb6c3357e864d8b07abd82c76d3ac38ab6d78598671733da7d28a9`

Visual conclusions came from inspecting saved SubViewport captures; XCTest success only confirms that foreground/lifecycle checks ran. The A/B was Debug on device. A Release patched object was built and checked, but that is not a Release device acceptance claim.

### Suspected mechanism and local fix

In [4.7.1 MDCommandBuffer::bind_pipeline](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a13da4feb8d8aefc283c3763d33a2f170a18d541/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp), changing the render pipeline marks uniforms dirty while `binding_cache.clear()` is commented out. Pipeline variants/sky shaders may use different direct-binding slots. Push constants are written using `setVertexBytes`/`setFragmentBytes` outside BindingCache, so a cached resource may no longer describe the actual contents of an encoder slot. The project diagnosis is that this can make subsequent transparent draws skip rebinding lighting resources. Upstream confirmation of the exact slot collision is still needed.

Our local change restores:
```cpp
binding_cache.clear();
render.mark_uniforms_dirty();
```
inside the `render.pipeline != rp` branch. Replacing the unique matching metal3_objects device archive member and relinking the App fixes the tested cases, without changing the PCK/shaders/colors/backend. Updating the PCK alone cannot apply this fix. The patch is attached for review; it is not an upstream-approved fix.

This report concerns the native binding-cache/transparent directional-light issue. The separate behavior of sky radiance not refreshing after global sky-color changes is outside its scope.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a physical iOS device, run a Mobile/Metal scene containing a ProceduralSkyMaterial background, a visible DirectionalLight3D (SKY_MODE_LIGHT_ONLY), opaque geometry, and an alpha-blended plane. Turn off glow, sky ambient lighting and reflections to isolate direct lighting.
2. Compare the transparent plane with the light enabled and disabled. In the tested fixtures, the transparent light contribution disappears after sky drawing, while the opaque plane remains lit. A builtin StandardMaterial3D alpha control also exhibited this in the original fixture.
3. Disable the sky background draw (use BG_COLOR) while keeping the light and materials. The transparent directional lighting returns in the tested fixture.
4. Restore binding_cache.clear() before render.mark_uniforms_dirty() on render-pipeline changes, rebuild the affected native object for the matching engine/target, and relink the same iOS App with the same PCK. The tested original scene renders correctly.
5. The attached asset-free diagnostic opens at diagnostic/project.godot. It shows six views (opaque/alpha, sky/no sky, light on/off), saves captures/report.json in an independent user directory, and prints linear light increments. This newly reduced project has NOT yet been independently run on iPhone; it is a diagnostic starting point. Removing the original opaque draws may change pipeline ordering, so it must not be taken as an already-verified standalone MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached: asset-free standalone diagnostic candidate, original numerical rendering evidence and the local 4.7.1 patch. It contains no game assets, account data, network services, plugins or GDExtensions.

[godot-metal-binding-diagnostic-20261005.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33042501/godot-metal-binding-diagnostic-20261005.zip)

**Validation boundary:** the evidence JSON files are from completed tests of the original isolated fixtures. The newly reduced standalone project is not yet independently device-validated; see README.md. The face A/B used project assets, which are not included. The original native export may include project extensions; a clean official export of this reduced project still needs verification.
